youtube.title: Aeschylus hid from a prophecy. A tortoise found him 🐢 #shorts
youtube.caption:
Aeschylus was told something would fall on him. So he never went indoors again. Smart, right? 🐢

Worst way to go in history? Drop yours 👇

Parody · fictional chat. Based on a legend: the Greek tragedian Aeschylus died in 456 BC. The Roman writer Valerius Maximus says an eagle, carrying a tortoise, mistook his bald head for a rock and dropped the tortoise on it to crack the shell. Pliny the Elder adds that he was staying out in the open because of a prophecy that he would be killed by a falling object. Historians treat the story as legend.
